(By Sri. A.N. Hegde.,Adv.,)
 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15.02.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 15.2.2023 at about 8.20 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing No. KA-01-EQ- 0648 as a pillion rider from Makali towards Goraguntepalya and when she reached NH-4 road on Peenya flyover, near Wadia Upper ramp at that time the rider of Royal Enfield two wheeler bearing No. KA-42-W- 7152 has ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Prakriya Hospital, after first aid she was shifted to Commando Hospital and she has spent more than Rs.1,50,000/-
towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and she was working as flower vendor and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue her work and is under complete bed rest and she is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, both the respondents appeared and filed their respective written statements.

Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel by admitting that he is the RC owner of the royal enfield two wheeler bearing No. KA-42-W-7152 and the same was insured with first respondent and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Also contended that at the time of accident, the rider of the said vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also alleged negligence.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against him.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-42-W-7152.

Further contended that, the Nalina vs Doreswamy S.B on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146528799/
2 accident was happened due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider.

sentences.text: Also contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further denied the age,
avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-W-7152 by its rider, in RTA took place on 15.2.2022 at about 8.20 a.m. on NH-4 road, Peenya flyover, Wadia upper ramp, National Highway, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 9.
Dr. Ramesh B who is working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P10 & 11.
In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents did not chose to adduce evidence.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed her affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of her case, she has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, wound certificate, spot mahazar, IMV report, and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Rohith who is the rider of the motor cycle in which the petitioner was travelling as pillion rider.

After the Nalina vs Doreswamy S.B on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146528799/
3 registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P4 spot mahazar was conducted.

It is the main allegation is that, when the petitioner was proceeding towards Goraguntepalya in motor cycle bearing No.
KA-01-EQ-0648, the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-42-W-7152 who was coming in the same direction dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner in which she was traveling as pillion rider.

In this regard, if we perused the contents of Ex.P4 mahazar and rough sketch appended therein, the accident spot is in the left side of the road and the rider of motor cycle bearing No.
KA-52-W-7152 has changed his lane and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner in which she was traveling as pillion rider.

Further, Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein no fresh damages were found on the offending motor cycle bearing No. KA-52-W-7152 but the right side crash guard of the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding has got damaged.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P4 mahazar and Ex.P5 IMV report establishes that the rider of offending motor cycle bearing No.
KA-52-W-7152 has changed his lane and dashed against the ahead going motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider.

The Ex.P4 mahazar and Ex.P5 IMV report helped the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-52-W-7152.
10.

Ex.P6 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.
KA-52-W-7152, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-42-W-7152.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner or the rider of the bike in which the petitioner was proceeding.
11. The respondent No.1 & 2 have filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-42- W-7152.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-42-W-7152.
12.

The charge sheet as per Ex.P6 came to be filed on the rider of motor cycle bearing No.
KA-42-W-7152 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC R/w. Sec. 134 (a& b) and 187 of IMV Act.

13. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

14. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by the negligence of rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA- 01-EQ-0648 nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.

15. The contents of Ex.P4 spot mahazar and Ex.P5 IMV report falsifies the contention of respondent no.2 about the contributory negligence of rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-EQ-0648 for the occurrence of accident.
In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 6
this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
16. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 15.2.2023 which is caused by the rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-42-W-7152 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
17.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 48 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P7 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 25.01.1975 hence, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 48 years.
In the petition itself she has averred that she was admitted to Prakriya Hospital and after first aid he was shifted to Commando Hospital.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 the petitioner sustained fracture shaft of clavicle( Lt.).

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.40,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P9, amounting to Rs.4,260/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same Nalina vs Doreswamy S.B on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146528799/
5 i.e., Rs.4,300/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that she was working as flower vendor and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to Prakriya Hospital and after first aid she was shifted to Commando Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient for four days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total three months period including 4 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 3 months = Rs.48,000/- during the laid up period.
d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by her the petitioner examined Dr. Ramesh B. Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2, through him OPD notes and X-ray are marked at Ex.P.10 & 11.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained left clavicle displaced fracture and she underwent treatment of internal fixation of (Lt) clavicle.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered permanent physical disability of 19% of left upper limb and whole body disability at 7%.
It is relevant to note that, Clavicle bone means (collarbone) is a long, slightly curved bone that connects your arm to your body.
The said bone can be found one on both sides of the base of the neck.
The bones help keep a shoulder blade in the correct position as a person move.
The word "clavicle" comes from the Latin "clavicula," which translates to "little key."
The bone is actually shaped a bit like an old-fashioned key.
And it works in much the same way.
When one rotate a key, it moves the lock.
Similarly, when a person lift a arm,a clavicle rotates along its axis to allow movement.

The clavicle, or collarbone, is a slender, S-shaped long bone approximately 6 inches (15 cm) long that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum (breastbone).There are two clavicles, one on the left and one on the right.
The clavicle is the only long bone in the body that lies horizontally.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder girdle.
It is a palpable bone and, in people who have less fat in this region, the location of the bone is clearly visible.
It receives its name from Latin clavicula 'little key' because the bone rotates along its axis like a key when the shoulder is abducted.
The clavicle is the most commonly fractured bone.
Itc an easily be fractured by impacts to the shoulder from the force of falling on outstretched arms or by a direct hit.
It is relevant to note that, Clavicle or collar bone is as lender S shaped bone approximately 6 inches that serves as as truth between the shoulder blade and the sternum.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder griddle.
To put it differently, clavicle bone is not a separate component of the arm but just a supporting bone.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 10% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Accordingly, no grounds are made out to show that the said injury caused the permanent disability and economical loss to the petitioner.

As such, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation Nalina vs Doreswamy S.B on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146528799/
6 under this head.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ; As per Ex.P8 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 4 days.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P3 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period she spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained she is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 4 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.4,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 4 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.35,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 40,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 4,300/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 48,000/-

d) Towards disability Rs. NIL e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 30,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 4,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 35,000/-
h) Towards future medical  expenses Rs. 30,000/-

7  _______________

Total Rs.1,91,300/-
 18. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Royal Enfield motor cycle bearing No. KA-42-W-7152 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,

Accordingly,
this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
19.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,91,300/-
(Rupees One lakh ninety one thousand three hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

rpc_texts: Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.35,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 40,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 4,300/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 48,000/-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,

this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
